beats.say: A razor costs $5. And you keep paying forever.
Buy the handle alone, no blades included.
Buy a starter kit with a few blades.
Buy the razor plus a subscription of endless blades.
First year: 51 razors, 168 blades. Sounds generous.
But it does a job: it locks you into blade buying.
The handle is a one-time $5 purchase.
Each blade costs extra, and the company sold 168 blades after just 51 handles.
In year two, razor sales exploded to 90,884, feeding a huge blade market.
You see it everywhere: a coffee shop sells a reusable cup for $5, but single-serve pods at $3 each.
A gym offers a starter bike for $200, then a $20 monthly class pass.
Now the recurring option feels smart because the cheap entry is just a hook.
Watch the cheap entry and count the repeat costs. Follow for more.
